html:
Shusha is a mountain town in Karabakh, founded around 1752 by Panah Ali Khan as the fortress capital of the Karabakh Khanate, one of the khanates that rose as Nader Shah's Iranian empire broke up.

It came under Russia in 1805. In the 1800s it grew into a centre of culture shared by Azerbaijanis and Armenians, and is called the cradle of Azerbaijani mugham music and poetry; Uzeyir Hajibeyov grew up there. In 1920 its Armenian quarter was burned in a massacre. Armenian forces took the town in 1992 during the Karabakh war, and its Azerbaijani people fled. Azerbaijan retook it in November 2020, the decisive victory of the Second Karabakh War.
sum: Shusha is a mountain town in Karabakh, founded around 1752 by Panah Ali Khan as the fortress capital of the Karabakh Khanate, one of the khanates that rose as Nader Shah's Iranian empire broke up.
